the question: how can we learn to master multiple sequential decision tasks at once?
the question: “How can a learning agent learn to solve multiple tasks at once, while maintaining generality and avoiding the distraction of certain tasks?”
the problem of training an agent that can solve multiple tasks simultaneously and efficiently.

our work demonstrates the feasibility of learning to master multiple sequential decision making tasks with a single agent and single set of weights, which is a major step forward in the quest to build general artificial intelligence.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to train a single agent to master many tasks simultaneously.
we have shown how to train a single deep reinforcement learning agent to solve multiple sequential decision tasks, and that this agent can outperform humans on all of them.
we have shown that it is possible to achieve state of the art multi-task reinforcement learning by adapting the contribution of each individual task to the learning dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multi-task reinforcement learning algorithms can achieve state-of-the-art performance in a variety of domains, and can be trained in a single shot.
